method: Use literal unbroken corpus words after typographic ligature expansion and NFC. Exclude code, formulas, figures, URLs, identifiers with underscores, and both halves of hyphenated line-wrap candidates. Preserve compounds attested with a hyphen; retain ambiguity until explicit review.
application_rules: Only normalize prose line-wrap boundaries; leave ordinary in-line hyphens, Code, formulas, URL destinations, and identifiers elsewhere untouched.
Prefer exact reviewed left/right pair overrides. The three identifier-pair repairs are limited to the hash-bound source nodes listed in scopes.

For remaining candidates, join only when the unhyphenated form occurs unbroken in this corpus and the hyphenated form does not. This is a corpus heuristic, not a manual review of all 2,515 such pairs.

Preserve an attested real compound or an ambiguous both-attested spelling unless an explicit reviewed override exists. In particular retain end-user, end-users, human-centered, human-centric, real-time, multi-touch, on-line, front-end, non-linear, and follow-up.
Retain an unattested pair unless explicitly reviewed. No new corpus token counts have been fabricated for reviewed additions.
Preserve casing by concatenating original fragments, never by substituting the lowercase matching key.
Expand only standard typographic ligatures and apply NFC before lexical comparison. Do not use global NFKC on technical notation.
Check the current source hashes against source_documents before reusing this dataset.
review_notes: The candidate extractor skips literal URLs, but fragments after a wrapped URL can remain in the candidate inventory; exclude URL-like source contexts before any automated joining and do not alter link destinations.

The 221 originally unattested pair types were screened. Explicit safe additions cover ordinary words and code-attested identifiers. The remainder includes real compounds, URLs, proper names requiring more evidence, and source extraction defects; it is not all erroneous hyphenation.

CFlow paragraph 487:0 and Cursor paragraph 322:0 contain superscripts interleaved into hyphenated words. Their reviewed transcriptions are in inline-notation-overrides.json; no lexical join rule can safely repair those extraction sequences.
